title: Dirichlet's Simultaneous Approximation Theorem from Minkowski
description: Derives Dirichlet's simultaneous Diophantine approximation theorem as a corollary of the parent Minkowski convex body theorem. For any finite family of reals α : Fin d → ℝ and any integer N ≥ 1, there exist an integer q with 1 ≤ q ≤ Nᵈ and integers p : Fin d → ℤ with |αᵢ·q - pᵢ| ≤ 1/N for all i. Mathlib contains only the one-dimensional Dirichlet theorem (via pigeonhole); the multi-dimensional version, obtained here from the geometry of numbers, is new.

meta.author: Lean Genius

mathlibDependencies.description: Lebesgue volume of an axis-aligned box ∏ Icc aᵢ bᵢ equals ∏ ofReal(bᵢ - aᵢ)
Determinant of an upper-triangular (BlockTriangular id) matrix is the product of its diagonal
|x - round x| ≤ 1/2 — used for the trivial N = 1 base case
Parent entry's Minkowski convex body theorem: a symmetric convex body of volume > 2ⁿ·covolume contains a nonzero lattice point

originalContributions: shearMatrix: the unipotent (d+1)×(d+1) shear matrix encoding simultaneous approximation; shearMatrix_det proves its determinant is 1 (covolume 1)
dirichletLattice: the lattice whose integer points are (q, p₀-α₀q, …, p_{d-1}-α_{d-1}q)
dirichletBox / boxVolume_eq: the symmetric box |x₀| ≤ Nᵈ+½, |xᵢ| ≤ 1/N with Lebesgue volume computed exactly via Real.volume_Icc_pi
boxVolume_gt_critical: the box volume 2^{d+1}(1 + 1/(2Nᵈ)) strictly exceeds the critical volume 2^{d+1}
dirichlet_minkowski_core: applies minkowski_fundamental and reads off a nonzero approximating lattice point with |q| ≤ Nᵈ (using integrality of Nᵈ to sharpen |q| ≤ Nᵈ+½)
dirichlet_simultaneous: the simultaneous Dirichlet theorem with 0 < q ≤ Nᵈ, obtained by a sign flip and a rounding base case at N = 1

overview.historicalContext: Dirichlet introduced his approximation theorem in 1842, and its simultaneous (multi-dimensional) form is one of the founding results of Diophantine approximation. Minkowski's 1889 geometry of numbers gave a geometric proof: the existence of good simultaneous rational approximations to α₁, …, α_d follows from the existence of a nonzero lattice point in a suitable symmetric convex box. This entry realizes exactly that derivation on top of the parent Minkowski formalization, answering its fifth open question.
overview.problemStatement: Open Question 5 of the parent entry asks: can Dirichlet's simultaneous-approximation theorem be derived as a corollary in this formalization, by applying minkowski_fundamental to the box {x : |xᵢ - αᵢx₀| < 1/Q for i ≥ 1, |x₀| ≤ Qⁿ} of covolume 1?
overview.proofStrategy: Work in ℝ^{d+1}. Build the unipotent shear matrix whose rows generate a covolume-1 lattice whose integer points are (q, p₀ - α₀q, …, p_{d-1} - α_{d-1}q). Form the symmetric box with half-widths Nᵈ+½ in coordinate 0 and 1/N in the rest; its Lebesgue volume is 2^{d+1}(1 + 1/(2Nᵈ)) > 2^{d+1} = 2^{d+1}·covolume. Minkowski's theorem yields a nonzero lattice point; reading off its coordinates and using that q and Nᵈ are integers sharpens |q| ≤ Nᵈ+½ to |q| ≤ Nᵈ. A sign flip makes q positive, and the degenerate N = 1 case is settled by rounding.
keyInsights: The skew of the lattice does the work: by using a unipotent shear lattice (determinant 1) against an axis-aligned box, the box volume is a trivial product ∏ widths via Real.volume_Icc_pi, while the lattice encodes the approximation geometry.

Slightly enlarging coordinate 0 to half-width Nᵈ+½ makes the box volume strictly exceed the critical 2^{d+1}, so the strict Minkowski theorem (rather than the harder boundary/compact version) suffices — and because Nᵈ is an integer, |q| ≤ Nᵈ+½ still forces the clean bound |q| ≤ Nᵈ.

The case q = 0 can only occur when N = 1: a nonzero lattice point with q = 0 has some integer pᵢ with 1 ≤ |pᵢ| ≤ 1/N, impossible for N ≥ 2. This isolates the only degenerate case, handled directly by rounding.

Mathlib already has the one-variable Dirichlet theorem (Real.exists_int_int_abs_mul_sub_le) proved by the pigeonhole principle; the genuinely new content here is the simultaneous version and its derivation from the convex body theorem.

sections.title: Overview: Dirichlet's simultaneous approximation theorem from Minkowski
sections.summary: Header docstring and imports: the open question, the simultaneous Diophantine approximation statement, the shear-matrix / covolume-1 lattice construction, the box-volume argument, honest scope, and references.
sections.mathContext: This file (open question minkowski-fundamental-theorem-oq-05) answers affirmatively whether Dirichlet's simultaneous approximation theorem can be derived as a corollary of the Minkowski convex body theorem. It proves: for every finite family α : Fin d → ℝ and integer N ≥ 1, there exist an integer q with 1 ≤ q ≤ Nᵈ and integers p : Fin d → ℤ with |αᵢ·q − pᵢ| ≤ 1/N for all i. Mathlib has the one-dimensional Dirichlet theorem (Real.exists_int_int_abs_mul_sub_le, by pigeonhole); the new content is the simultaneous multi-dimensional version obtained as a corollary of the parent's minkowski_fundamental, exactly as the open question requests. The header docstring (lines 1–70) gives the Minkowski construction: in ℝ^{d+1} take the lattice generated by the rows of the unipotent shear matrix (1 on the diagonal, −αᵢ in the top row), determinant 1 so covolume 1; a lattice point (q, p₀−α₀q, …) inside the symmetric box |x₀| ≤ Nᵈ+½, |xᵢ| ≤ 1/N of volume 2^{d+1}(1 + 1/(2Nᵈ)) > 2^{d+1}·covolume is produced by Minkowski's theorem; reading off coordinates and using |q| ≤ Nᵈ+½ ⇒ |q| ≤ Nᵈ (q integer) yields the approximation, with a sign flip for q > 0 and the q = 0 case (only at N=1) handled by rounding. HONEST SCOPE (as the docstring states): 0 sorries, 0 new axioms — a genuine reduction to minkowski_fundamental (itself from Mathlib's geometry-of-numbers API) plus Real.volume_Icc_pi and the upper-triangular determinant. References: Dirichlet (1842), Cassels (1959).

sections.title: The Shear Matrix and Its Lattice
sections.summary: Defines the unipotent shear matrix (identity except row 0, off-diagonal -αⱼ), proves it is upper triangular and has determinant 1, and packages it as dirichletLattice with covolume 1.

sections.title: The Symmetric Box and Its Volume
sections.summary: Defines boxHi (half-widths Nᵈ+½ and 1/N), the ConvexBody dirichletBox = Icc(-boxHi, boxHi), computes its Lebesgue volume exactly via Real.volume_Icc_pi, and proves it exceeds the critical volume 2^{d+1}.

sections.title: Minkowski Core: A Nonzero Approximating Point
sections.summary: Helper lemmas evaluate the shear-matrix entries; dirichlet_minkowski_core applies minkowski_fundamental, reads off the lattice point's coordinates as q and p, derives |q| ≤ Nᵈ and the approximation bounds, and proves the point is nonzero.

sections.title: Dirichlet's Simultaneous Approximation Theorem
sections.summary: dirichlet_simultaneous handles N = 1 by rounding, and for N ≥ 2 uses the core point with a sign flip to deliver 0 < q ≤ Nᵈ and |αᵢ·q - pᵢ| ≤ 1/N.

conclusion.summary: Proves Dirichlet's simultaneous Diophantine approximation theorem with 0 sorries and 0 axioms (depending only on propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound), as a genuine corollary of the parent Minkowski convex body theorem. The result extends Mathlib's one-dimensional Dirichlet theorem to arbitrarily many simultaneous approximations.
conclusion.implications: The derivation confirms that the parent's custom Minkowski infrastructure is strong enough to recover classical number-theoretic consequences of the geometry of numbers. The same construction (shear lattice + axis-aligned box) is the template for further corollaries such as the Hurwitz/Liouville-type bounds and the theory of best simultaneous approximations.
openQuestions: Can the boundary (compact) Minkowski theorem be used to obtain the sharper bound with strict inequality |αᵢ·q - pᵢ| < 1/N for the inhomogeneous case?
Can the badly-approximable / Khintchine transference principles be formalized on top of this simultaneous statement?
Can the dual form (simultaneous approximation of a single linear form) be derived by transposing the shear lattice?
